name: plan-phases-project-scoping
body:
`apg_plan_phases` (the suite tool `opencode-suite/tools/apg_plan_phases.ts`) reports exactly the requirements the current project/branch is responsible for. The tool loads the `Requirement` nodes from the layers store and flags each requirement lacking a `Satisfies` edge as unsatisfied. A project's plan is transient and dies with its branch, so a requirement delivered by another project has an empty surviving `Satisfies` set; scoping the requirement set to the project keeps those requirements out of the finding.

IN SCOPE: a requirement is in scope for the current project/branch when it is BRANCH-ADDED or is SATISFIED by one of this project's phases — in-scope = branch-added requirements ∪ requirements this project's phases Satisfy. Branch-added means a `apg/layers/requirements/requirement/<name>.json` node file present on this branch but absent from the repo's default branch; the binary computes the analogous merge-base durable-spec delta in `rust.apg.plan_cmd.verify.change_set_spec_delta` (`src/plan_cmd/verify.rs`). The suite tool may shell out to git to compute this (the shared lib already runs subprocesses via `Bun.$` for `apg query`). The design splits cleanly across the test tiers: the scoping decision is a PURE function in the shared `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts` — given the full requirement FQN set, the branch-added set, and this project's `Satisfies` phase FQNs, it returns the in-scope set and the findings — and is covered by the bun unit tier in `opencode-suite/lib/apg.test.ts`; the git branch-delta shell-out is a thin subprocess WRAPPER around that pure core (a subprocess is real I/O, hence e2e) and is covered by the opt-in suite e2e. The tool's top-level logic is a default-exported `tool({...})` and works outside direct unit-test; the pure core lives in the shared lib.

FINDINGS:
- The tool reports the empty-tasks finding, the done-but-under-review finding, and the Gates-cycle finding.
- `!! unsatisfied requirements` = in-scope requirements lacking a `Satisfies` edge from a phase of this project (equivalently, branch-added requirements the project's plan leaves unsatisfied).
- `!! <req> Satisfied by more than one phase` = requirements Satisfied by more than one phase of this project (the `Satisfies` lookup filtered to this project's phases).

ACCEPTANCE:
- Running `apg_plan_phases` in a project whose branch adds zero requirement and whose plan satisfies its own requirements reports zero unsatisfied finding for requirements delivered by other projects; the in-scope set is exactly {requirements added on this branch} ∪ {requirements this project's phases Satisfy}.
- A branch-added requirement lacking a satisfying phase is reported unsatisfied; a requirement satisfied by two phases of the project is reported over-satisfied.
- The tool reports the empty-tasks, done-but-under-review, and Gates-cycle findings.
- Test tiers, split exactly: the PURE scoping core in `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts` (requirement FQNs + branch-added set + this project's `Satisfies` phase FQNs -> in-scope set and findings) is covered by the side-effect-free bun unit tier in `opencode-suite/lib/apg.test.ts`; the git branch-delta shell-out wrapper is covered by the opt-in suite e2e (`opencode-suite/tests/boundary.e2e.test.ts`) against a scratch `/tmp` repo per the self-contained-tests law.
- `full_dogfood_round_trip_suite_tool_ops_inside_the_worktree` (`tests/project_cmd_e2e.rs`) and `suite_tools_query_error_guard_is_structural` (`tests/main_e2e.rs`, which structurally pins `apg_plan_phases.ts`'s try/catch/`csvToRows`/return shape) pass.
- Non-goal: the `apg` binary and suite tools other than `apg_plan_phases` and the shared-lib helper it uses stay untouched (see `requirements.constraint.plan-tooling-change-boundary`).

CONSEQUENCE: `opencode-suite/agents/plan-writer.md` relies on `apg_plan_phases` reporting unsatisfied requirements for its self-review; that check is project-local.
